IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01792

Yet as far as the world beyond is concerned, the person whose spiritual growth stops here remains “primitive.” Such people, Semnânî says, are found in deserts, at sea, and on islands; they do not yet meet the standard of human beings (qâ’ida-ye âdamiyân).
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01793

2) The second possibility under case (b) marks a higher level. Here the subtle organism receives a dominant influence coming jointly from the Sphere of Spheres and the Soul of the universe (the Throne, ’Arsh), together with a lesser influence received directly, without intermediary, from Intelligence (’Aql). These three influences combine with the element Earth to form the second subtle center or organ, called the latîfa nafsîya (the subtle organ at the level of the vital soul). In the growth of the subtle body, this is the Noah of your being.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01794

For, as we saw earlier, this latîfa is the esoteric meaning of all the revealed accounts in which Noah appears, and it is at this level that those accounts must be inwardly understood. The person belonging to this latîfa possesses civilization, culture, and religious worship, though not in conformity with religion in its truth. The aura by which this latîfa is recognized in visionary experience is blue—even though, together with the preceding latîfa, it is classified as lacking color.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01795
We can detect here a visual perception that scarcely distinguishes blue from black.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01796

3) The third latîfa takes us back to case (a) within the larger alternative B): a subtle organ that is not inherently luminous but is characterized by a certain color. Its substance is formed by influences combining with the element Earth. The dominant influence emanates from the four proto-substances and, consequently, from the Intelligence from which they proceed. A lesser influence comes from one of the four “first realities” (awwaliyât), the one called the “luminous Ink”—that is, the Muhammadan Light (Nûr mohammadî). This is the subtle organ or center at the level of the heart (latîfa qalbîya).
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01797

We saw earlier that it is within this latîfa that the “spiritual child,” the true Self, takes shape as an embryo. As the father of this child, this spiritual organ is the Abraham of your being. The person belonging to this latîfa is the devout Muslim, not yet wholly steadfast, still tossed between dawn and dusk, between fidelity and rebellion. The colored covering, the aura of this subtle organ, is red.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01798

4) Let us return to hypothesis (A), set out above, concerning those latîfas, or subtle centers, that are luminous by their very nature. Here again there are two possibilities: (a) the spiritual seeker has attained the state of the Perfect Human Being, or (b) has not yet attained it fully. In the latter case, the subtle organ is constituted by two kinds of influx. The predominant influx is itself twofold, flowing from the four primordial substances and from the first reality called the Ink of Light. The lesser influx proceeds from the first reality called the Inkwell, that is, the Muhammadan Spirit (Rûh mohammadî). When these influxes combine with the element of Earth, transforming and refining it, they give rise to the subtle organ known as the latîfa sirrîya: the subtle center of the sirr, literally the “secret,” the innermost heart, beyond ordinary consciousness. This is the Moses of your being, the organ through which intimate conversations (monâjât) with God take place and their hidden meaning is understood. The person who has reached this center is the mu’min, the fully realized believer. Notice again the progression from moslim to mu’min: professing Islam is still only the husk or outer shell; îmân, inward faith, is the flesh and the kernel. Such a person belongs among those called a “Friend of God” (walî), conventionally translated as a “saint.” Here we encounter once more the question raised earlier: how does the Sufi idea of wilâyat, the spiritual standing of God's friends, relate to the Shiite conception of walâyat, which remains the key to the entire structure? The aura of this latîfa is white.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01799

5) Let us now return to possibility (a) in the preceding paragraph. Two further cases must be distinguished: (A) the seeker has needed initiation from another human being, someone like himself; or (B) the seeker has had no human master but has been initiated directly by an Angel. In case (A), the subtle organ is formed by the following influxes. First comes the predominant influx, composed of three streams arising respectively from the four primordial substances and from two of the first realities: the Ink of Light, or Muhammadan Light, and the Inkwell, or Muhammadan Spirit. A lesser influx proceeds from the first of the first realities: the Most Holy Pen (Qalam qodsî). Together these influxes produce the subtle organ called the latîfa rûhîya, the center of the Spirit (rûh, pneuma). This is the David of your being. The person at this station possesses the virtues of a fully realized Friend of God (Walî). He is a spiritual guide (walî morshid), the “Pole of Perfect Guidance” (Qotb-e irshâd-e tâmm). The light, or aura, announcing this latîfa is yellow.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01800

6) Possibility (B) in the preceding paragraph concerns the seeker who has reached perfection without needing a human master. The distinctions Semnâni now introduces to define the types in his mystical anthropology are precisely those which, in Shiite teachings on prophecy—particularly those transmitted by Kolaynî—determine the kinds of knowledge, and hence the divisions of a theory of knowledge underlying the hierarchy of prophets and Imams. The seeker with no human master has been initiated directly into knowledge of the unseen (’olûm-e ghayb) by the angel Gabriel, the Angel of Revelation. But here a further distinction arises: (a) he sees the Angel while awake, or (b) he sees the Angel only in dreams. In the latter case, the subtle organ at work is formed by two influxes. The predominant one combines the streams proceeding from the four primordial substances and the four first realities, and therefore ultimately from the Most Holy Pen, the source of these first principles. The lesser influx comes from the divine attribute of Light, marking the “third descent” of being discussed above. This Light pours into the latîfa through the mediation of the First Intelligence. The result is the subtle organ called the latîfa khafîya, the hidden center of the arcanum, or innermost mystery. This is the Jesus of your being. As we have already seen, he announces the name of the last prophet in the cycle and therefore the last “prophet of your being,” the “seal of your being.” That is why the color marking this next-to-last enclosure, immediately before the final height—or depth—of hidden meanings, is luminous black: a night that is not darkness, a union of opposites recalling the “midnight sun” that set Hermes ablaze with ecstasy, as Suhrawardî emphasized. The person at this center is a prophet, a nabî simply, meaning a prophet who has not also been entrusted with the mission of a Messenger.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01801

7) With possibility (a) from the preceding paragraph, we reach the supreme latîfa. This is the case of a prophet who needs no human master, receives initiation directly from the Angel, and sees the Angel not merely in dreams but while awake. The organ of this vision is the latîfa haqqîya, the “divine subtle organ.” We have seen that it is called the Muhammad of your being: the subtle center containing the pearl of your true Self, whose embryo begins to form in the subtle center of the heart and which is the spiritual offspring of the “Abraham of your being.” Yet here, once more, we encounter the distinctions familiar from the Imams' teachings on prophecy as reported by Kolaynî. The preceding paragraph concerned the nabî who is a prophet but not a Messenger. A prophet may, however, also be a Messenger (nabî-morsal). Moreover, a Messenger may be sent with a Book and a Revelation destined one day to be superseded; or he may be the last Messenger, the “Seal of the Prophets,” entrusted with delivering the final Revelation.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01802

(a) When a prophet is not charged with founding a new religion, but receives the Angel's teaching directly and is sent on a mission to a people, a city, a family, or even the smallest group, he is a prophet-messenger (nabî-morsal). In the typology, he represents the initial state of the latîfa haqqîya.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01803

At this first stage the “divine subtle organ” is formed by the following influxes: a predominant stream arising from the four primordial substances, the four first realities, and the divine Light mediated by the First Intelligence; and a lesser stream from the divine Life which marks the “second descent” of being. This Life is transmitted through the First Intelligence, acting as the “deputy,” or khalîfa, of the primordial Center: the absolute oneness of the pure Essence.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01804

(b) When a prophet is charged with bringing a new revelation and establishing a new religion, he belongs to the group known as the ulû’l-’azm, prophets entrusted with a divine undertaking of exceptional resolve. Here, too, there are two cases. In the first, the prophet is one of those through whom the cycle of prophecy unfolds. He is one manifestation of the “True Prophet,” a conception that arose in Jewish-Christian Ebionite thought and bore such fruit in Islam that, for Semnâni, it marks the successive phases of mystical experience.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01805

But because this prophet represents only one moment in the prophetic cycle, his manifestation will in turn be superseded by the next prophet. He symbolizes the middle state of the “divine subtle organ.” At this stage the organ is formed by a predominant influx combining the streams from the four primordial substances, the four first realities, and pre-eternal Light and Life—the third and second “descents” of being. To these is added a lesser influx of Being, corresponding to the first “descent” of being, which reaches the organ through the First Intelligence, mediator of the “center of the pure Essence” (noqtat dhâtîya).
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01806

(c) In the second case, the prophet is the “Seal of the Prophets.” The revelation he brings, and the religion he establishes, will never be abrogated. In the terms of Jewish-Christian theories of prophecy, the “True Prophet” has reached his “place of rest.” This prophet represents the completed and final state of the latîfa haqqîya. Here, in perfect harmony, every influx previously mentioned is present in equal measure: those arising from the four primordial substances and the four first realities, together with the threefold radiance of Light, Life, and Being which the Intelligence sends forth as mediator of the “center of oneness” of the pure Essence.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01807

Through the union of these subtle influxes, the latîfa haqqîya develops into the latîfat al-anâ’îya, the subtle organ of the true Self, of personhood in its true sense (anâ’îyat haqqîya). Born in the “subtle center of the heart,” it has drawn to itself, from latîfa to latîfa, by its own magnetic power, the substance of the worlds of malakût, jabarût, and lâhût. At its final degree, it is the mirror of the divine Face in all its beauty and majesty.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01808

The “acquired subtle body” is its incorruptible covering, inseparable from it, just as the earthly body in this world is the covering of that “acquired subtle body.” Such is the “Seal of the Prophets, beloved of the Lord of the worlds, quintessence of all beings, pearl in the shell of the world of contingency, perfect fruit borne by the tree planted in the orchard of the visible world. By the sun of his prophecy and the moon of his walâyat, he illuminates the heavens of the horizons and the souls.”
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01809

In the “world of the horizons,” this praise concerns Muhammad the Chosen One, Seal of the Prophets. In the “world of the soul,” it concerns the “Muhammad of your being,” the “Seal of the prophets of your being”: the latîfa haqqîya, the divine subtle organ enclosing, like a shell, the pearl of your true Self, the spiritual child of the “Abraham of your being,” conceived in the subtle center of the heart. The color of this center is emerald green, growing brighter as the latîfa draws nearer to its completed, final state.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01810

Yet we already know that the unfolding of the hidden meaning of this final prophecy can have no end. That is precisely the Shiite insight, and, when prophecy is understood as something taking place within the soul, it is Semnâni's secret.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01811

IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)

What is a lesser influx at one level becomes part of the predominant influx at the next. The first two latîfas are still affected by the influx of the Sphere of Spheres; at the third this is eliminated. The influx of the Intelligence, still secondary at the second center, becomes predominant at the third. The Ink of Light, still a lesser influence at the third, becomes predominant at the fourth.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01814

And so it continues. In succession come the influxes of the primordial substances, the first realities, and the highest epiphanic qualifications of being, until all are gathered in equal measure in the seventh latîfa. Every principle analyzed by Semnâni's meticulous metaphysics of being thus plays an actual part in forming the organs of the human subtle body, through a progressive transformation of the original earthly element.

We use this term again, as we did for Rûzbehân in Book III, because the material is both remarkably similar and, in another sense, quite different. Here too we have a “spiritual diary” recording a series of visionary experiences (earlier we also mentioned Swedenborg's).
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01819

Yet Rûzbehân, at a friend's request, gathered the contents of his diary into a single book. Semnâni did not. His accounts are scattered throughout his writings, and someone would have to bring them together to reconstruct his Diarium spirituale—a task we cannot undertake here.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01820

We can at least offer a glimpse of some of its contents. We may expect them to provide the confirmation of experience for the account just given. They concern the growth of the subtle body's organs, the ascent from one latîfa to another, and the awareness of what occurs at each level: above all, the perception of an aura whose color reveals to the visionary how far his true Self has grown within its imperishable subtle body. Semnâni confides his trials and doubts, his visions of lights, and his many experiences of perception beyond the ordinary senses.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01821

Yet when the moment comes to disclose the “ultimate secret,” he holds back; he “rolls up the carpet.” He does not consider himself entitled to say more, leaving us to approach the experience only from some distance.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01822

We have just used the word “event” (wâqi’a), a characteristic term in Semnâni's technical vocabulary. It must be understood in the very sense his Qur'anic commentary, or Tafsîr, gives it when interpreting the surah that bears this title: surah 56, al-Wâqi’a. It is generally translated “the Event.” But the ordinary word lacks sufficient force.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01823

What is meant is a visionary event, an encounter with the unseen through every form of mystical perception. At each turning point in the mystic's inner life, the event carries the full eschatological meaning associated with it in the Qur'an, for each such event contains the idea of a resurrection. This becomes entirely clear from Semnâni's commentary on two neighboring surahs: surah 54, on the splitting of the Moon, which we saw earlier allowed Sâ’inoddîn ’Alî Torkeh Ispahânî to sketch his own hierarchy and typology of spiritual seekers; and surah 56, the Event. In his Tafsîr, Semnâni relates the “approaching Hour” (al-sâ’at, 54:1) and the visionary Event to two different latîfas, according to the depth of the hidden meaning that each can reach. For each subtle organ has its own resurrection, designated by a particular Qur'anic term.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01824

The resurrection announced by surah 54—“The Hour drew near and the Moon was split” (54:1)—concerns the center of the heart (latîfa qalbîya). It is the third center in the ascending order, the “Abraham of your being,” because it carries the embryo of your spiritual posterity: your own child, your true Self. Struck by a flash of divine inspiration, the mystic now finds himself, in the “world of his soul,” in the Prophet's own situation: his people rise against him.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01825

“If they see a Sign, they turn away and exclaim: This is an unending spell of magic.” Here the rebellious people are the psychic faculties belonging to the first two subtle organs—the people of the “Adam of your being” and the “Noah of your being,” enveloped respectively in dark black and blue fluorescence. These faculties represent unbelievers and deniers who use rationally established knowledge to demonstrate the impossibility of what their prophet announces. “They call him a liar. Before them, Noah's people had already cried imposture” (54:3, 9).
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01826

In the inner reading, this refers to the time when the latîfa nafsîya, purified of its stains, was sent to those lower powers of your being with “manifest Signs.” “So turn away from them” (54:6). Through ta’wîl, the inward interpretation, this command is addressed to the “Muhammad of your being”: turn away from those who cannot die before their bodily death, and who therefore remain strangers to the conditions of spiritual resurrection. Semnâni even coins a term made possible by Arabic.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01827

Since the angel Isrâfîl, or Seraphiel, is the angel of resurrection, the call to the “Seraphiel-like power” (isrâfîlîyat) of the “prophets of your being” inevitably makes the doubting, calculating, denying faculties recoil in helpless terror. Surah 56 then sounds the answering note of a resurrection belonging to the center of the Spirit (latîfa rûhîya), the fifth latîfa, the “David of your being.” “When it comes, the mountains shake, and the earth trembles like the surface of a sea stirred by waves; the fires of desire and Eros blaze beneath the victorious breath of grace, brought by the north wind of beauty.”
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01828

The event is decisive. Once it occurs, nothing and no one can cast doubt on it. When the mystic opens his eyes again upon the world accessible to the senses, he understands that, compared with this visionary event, everything he had previously seen in the visible world was seen as though in a dream. Hence the Prophet's saying: “Human beings are asleep; when they die, they awaken.”
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01829

With the resurrection of the latîfa rûhîya, the eyes are opened to visions in which the divine becomes manifest. Reading the commentaries on these two surahs together allows us to understand the full meaning of wâqi’a in Semnâni. “The wâqi’a,” he writes, “the event or encounter, consists in your vision perceiving something in the supersensible world (al-ghayb). Your vision means this: that when you open your eyes, you see something in the sensory world, certainly, but as though you were seeing it in the supersensible world (nahwa mâ tarâ-ho fi’l ghayb).”
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01830

These words express with exceptional clarity the very secret of theophanic perception: a vision that apprehends sensible things while simultaneously “seeing” them in the mundus imaginalis, the imaginal world, as they truly are in their spiritual state, invisible to our outward senses. For a sensible form is true only when its spiritual counterpart is perceived. This is the very process of visionary experience, and we could cite converging testimonies here, from Ibn ’Arabî as well as Swedenborg. For Semnâni, the wâqi’a is a compelling confirmation through experience of the great principle underlying his ta’wîl, his esoteric interpretation: that meaning must be discovered inwardly.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01831

All visible forms in the “outer or exoteric world of the horizons” (’âlam al-âfâq) are, at the same time, forms of the soul's attributes or modes of being in the “inner or esoteric world of souls” (’âlam al-anfos). Otherwise, we could know nothing of the soul's modes of being and could not rise from one mystical station (maqâm) to another. The inward discovery of meaning must therefore occur as the growth of the subtle body, an ascent from latîfa to latîfa, and the mystic must be able to see his inner states. Semnâni experienced this throughout his life, yet he does not conceal the doubts he had to overcome. That candor is surely one of his most valuable lessons.
IV. The Seven Subtle Organs of the Human Being According to 'Ala al-Dawla Semnani (d. 1336)
passage-en-01832

Something perceived by a visionary in the “world of mystery” (’âlam al-ghayb), he explains, may become manifest in the visible world. The visible and the invisible belong together “as one sandal matches another.” The problem is the same when an inner state is given an imaginal form within an aura of a particular color. The spiritual masters want to verify that what appears to them—not through the outward senses, but through inward imaginative perception—is indeed the outward Form, the apparentia realis, the real manifestation of an invisible or “hidden” spiritual reality (sûrat al-ma’nâ al-ghaybî), and that this Figure bears truthful witness to what exists in the “world of mystery.”
